chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Joe Smith and Pike Davis, trumpet players
summary: Danny and Milt discuss Russell's brother Joe Smith, who mesmerized with his trumpet, and Pike Davis, a pit-band trumpeter and rival of Johnny Dunn.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: His brother was a great trumpet player, Joe Smith. I didn't know if you knew him.

Joe Smith... Well, I didn't know him either. I saw him once. He went to Kansas City with the Cotton-Pickers, McKinney's Cotton Pickers, and he met a woman out there and he stayed out there for six months. Some big sportin' woman. 'Cause he was a cat could mesmerize you with that trumpet. Joe Smith, yeah.
Yeah. He was in Kelly's Hot Chocolates and those shows. I remember Andy Smith used to talk about him, and another guy named Pike Davis. Did you know Pike?

Yeah, Pike Davis. Yeah, I used see Pike all the time. Pike Davis was a trumpet player who was a rival of Johnny Dunn. He used to be the first trumpet player in the branch of them Broadway shows. They know how to play with that dead tone. They don't use no vibrato in those shows, in that pit.

Straight tone, in there with that... And I used to see... I saw Joe Smith a couple of times, when the Cotton Pickers came to town. He went to Kansas City and met that woman and died out there. [JOE SMITH MOVED TO K.C. IN 1931, BUT LEFT WITH FLETCHER HENDERSON CIRCA 1936(?), AND DIED IN NYC IN DECEMBER 1937]
